items.title: Elon Musk now has an unfathomable amount of money. It looks a bit like this
items.description: Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire. It is hard to fathom a figure so staggering, but let's give it a shot.

items.title: Breaking: Woman suffers critical injuries after shark attack in Sydney's east
items.description: A woman is in a critical condition after being bitten by a shark at a beach in Sydney's east.

items.title: Tony Abbott is back in town and the fallout is biblical
items.description: Tony Abbott has been back in the political cycle for barely a fortnight and already the air is redolent with garment-rending, ancient feuds, biblical comeuppance and a listening tour.

items.title: Trump says US has killed leader of Venezuelan drug cartel in air strike
items.description: The US president said he would continue to track down Tren de Aragua members and "send them to the depths of hell where they belong".

items.title: Trump says ceasefire deal 'close', but it could be on Iran's terms
items.description: Amid rising expectations a pathway to peace between Iran and the US is close, the reported details of a ceasefire deal appear to show Iran getting numerous concessions from the White House.

items.title: Live: US running rampant in three-goal first half against Paraguay
items.description: World Cup co-host USA gets its campaign underway against Paraguay after Canada rescued a late draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina in Toronto. Follow live.

items.title: Why we cannot name high-profile man at centre of extortion case
items.description: There is a highly secretive and unusual court case playing out behind closed doors in Far North Queensland involving a prominent married man and his alleged affair, a non-publication order we are not allowed to see and an allegation of extortion we cannot tell you much about.

items.title: 'Seeking connection': The unseen children who roam the streets at night
items.description: Youth Beat workers take to Perth streets at night to help young people who have nowhere else to go.

items.title: Are you one of Australia's 1.1 million 'power couples'? Here's how you know
items.description: The ranks of Australia's so-called power couples, in which both partners are university-educated, have almost quadrupled over 20 years. This could have profound implications for social inequality.

items.title: 'Lambo Guy' Adrian Portelli sues former minister over lottery comments
items.description: Melbourne "rewards club" lottery billionaire Adrian Portelli has launched a defamation lawsuit against former SA minister Andrea Michaels over comments she made about a $3.5 million home prize draw.

items.title: They know it looks unusual, but these mates are 'piggybacking the world'
items.description: Best friends Lachie and Fletcher have nailed the art of ignoring what people think, travelling the world as Two Mates, 1 Chair.

items.title: Could Switzerland become the first country to restrict its population?
items.description: The Swiss will go to the polls on Sunday to vote on whether to back a referendum that would see its population capped at 10 million.

items.title: A man fled a 'bounty' in Canberra. Months later, he was dead in Brisbane
items.description: Neil Tracey's death was ruled an overdose in what investigators would call an open and shut case. His family are questioning if police knew about the bounty that led him to flee his hometown.

items.title: Trump's name set to be stripped from Kennedy Center as appeal fails
items.description: With storms dancing around Washington before a court-ordered deadline to remove references to Donald Trump, workers were seen building scaffolding around a section of the building that includes the president's name.

items.title: Britain's defence strategy under fire while global nuclear spending surges
items.description: The prospect of nuclear weapons being used in either Ukraine or the Middle East, rather than being fired between Moscow, Washington or Beijing has risen.

items.title: The highs and lows of having a pet
items.description: Pets can be lifelong companions, but they can also test us in ways we never imagined. We asked you to share your stories. Here's what you told us.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Testing your knowledge of ABBA, the World Cup mascots and some fruity language
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right; the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Taylor Swift, Alanis Morissette inducted into Songwriters Hall of Fame
items.description: Taylor Swift has become the youngest woman to be inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. She's among the writers behind some of pop's biggest hits to be inducted in 2026.

items.title: Grandfather of child rescued from Syria pleads for 'stability, love, care'
items.description: Jasmine was five years old and so traumatised that when she woke up trying to scream, she couldn't make a sound.

items.title: Australia has valuable cards to play in the AI future, new report finds
items.description: A new report says Australia can capitalise on AI, with valuable cards to play strategically.

items.title: How Israel's operation 'Eternal Darkness' in southern Lebanon is expanding
items.description: The so-called ceasefire since April, which Hezbollah is not a party to, has done little to halt the death and destruction in southern Lebanon. Here's how the scale of the Israeli operation called "Eternal Darkness" continues to expand.

items.title: Parents create 'university of life' for non-verbal daughter

items.title: The sword that links feared pirates to Britain's greatest naval hero
items.description: The history of a wavy-bladed sword, bought at a Brisbane gun show around the end of the 1980s, begins with Moro raiders resisting Spanish colonists in the Philippines, but may also include Admiral Lord Nelson.

items.title: New ambassador to US takes up tariffs, AUKUS causes
items.description: Greg Moriarty says he will "robustly" push back on the Trump administration's "extremely disappointing" new tariff plan and may recruit Australian businesses to help take up the fight.

items.title: Villages 700 years old destroyed to 'uproot people' from their history
items.description: Non-governmental organisations Biladi and Blue Shield are among the design experts using new technologies to create detailed records of cultural heritage and help rebuild after conflict.
